processing_notes: WHO annual cholera surveillance database shows zero cases reported for GNQ in all years prior to 2005. The 2005 epidemic (946 cases, 15 deaths) is the sole recorded event. Evidence type: Documented_Absence from WHO primary surveillance record. Note: BMC Public Health Cameroon study (doi:10.1186/s12889-025-23007-5) independently states 'Equatorial Guinea last reported in 2005' as a contextual aside, corroborating this absence.

That claim is falsified by the Level 1 baseline ./data/GNQ/cholera_data_jhu.csv, a digitisation of the same WHO annual reports (UID 320, Phantom: False): 1984 = 404 cases/31 deaths, 1985 = 108/1, 2004 = 59/1. Source hierarchy (CLAUDE.md): WHO official annual figures > an AI summary that misread the database. The remaining years (1980-83, 1986-2003) lose their only basis: a WHO table that omits a non-reporting country is not a reported zero, and GNQ surveillance functioning in 1980-2003 is undocumented while neighbours (Cameroon, Nigeria) had epidemics, so neither Documented_Absence nor Inferred_Absence is supported. The row was rendering ~22 years of false documented_zero (conf 0.85) in cholera_weekly_GNQ.csv. Rejected alternatives: (a) narrowing to 1980-83 + 1986-2003 as Documented_Absence - no source; (b) relabelling Inferred_Absence - system-operational criterion unmet. Agents 1/3/4/6 tasked to re-establish 1980-2003 from WER annual tables.
